title: Chile · Andes and Cajón del Maipo
slogan: A 174 km loop out of San José de Maipo
story: High Andes scenery close enough to feel unreal. This road trip is shaped as a ride, not as a shortcut: leave the start cleanly, use the first checkpoint for fuel and weather discipline, then let the middle 70 km be the part you remember. The best part sits around Embalse El Yeso, Baños Morales, while Pirque return and San José de Maipo keep the day practical instead of turning it into a fuel hunt. Check the selected map before departure: scenic sections, transfer sections, speed/control reminders, risk points and the GPX checkpoint order are deliberately visible so the route is understandable before the engine starts. Ride it early if the area is popular, keep the photo stops legal, and shorten the route if weather, daylight or energy stops agreeing with the plan.

sections.advice: Use Santiago start → San José de Maipo (41 km) as clean positioning. Keep it tidy, ignore impatient traffic and save the enthusiasm for the good road ahead. The value here is not drama; it is arriving at the riding section with space, fuel and concentration intact.

sections.advice: This Embalse El Yeso → Baños Morales stretch is for rhythm and scenery. Keep your head up, let the view breathe, and resist turning every open bend into a target. Stop once properly rather than half-stopping everywhere.

sections.advice: Baños Morales → Pirque return (18 km) is the reward section in Santiago. Look through the bends, use legal pull-offs for photos and keep a little margin for tractors, cyclists and damp shade. The best ride here is smooth, not noisy.

scenicChapters.title: Cajón del Maipo
scenicChapters.narrative: Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast. For 38 km this is Cajón del Maipo, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it.
